title: Native Extension Buffers and Unbounded Resource Processing
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library (ctypes, struct, io, zlib); int/str conversion limit requires Python 3.11+ (sys.set_int_max_str_digits)
security_mechanism: ctypes and struct trust caller-declared sizes: a length taken from input drives ctypes.memmove / create_string_buffer / a struct.unpack format, so a mismatch between the declared and real buffer size writes past the allocation or misreads adjacent memory. io's read() with no argument loads the entire stream into memory, zlib/gzip decompress output without an output cap turns a small compressed upload into gigabytes (decompression bomb), and int<->str conversion is quadratic; before Python 3.11's conversion limit an attacker-supplied huge integer makes serialization burn CPU indefinitely.

source_sink_clues.source: Content-Length or declared sizes from protocol headers, compressed upload bodies, serialized integers, and binary payloads fed to struct/ctypes.
source_sink_clues.sink: ctypes memory APIs sized from input; struct.unpack with input-derived formats; file/socket .read() with no cap; zlib/bz2/lzma decompress without output limits; int(str)/str(int) on attacker-sized values

tracking_guards: Check every input-derived length against a fixed constant before use; check reads use read(n) with n bounded; check decompression is incremental with an output-byte budget; check the interpreter enforces sys.set_int_max_str_digits (3.11+) where attacker integers are converted.
not_candidate_when: The transport already caps body size below the guard threshold and that cap is enforced before parsing, buffers are sized from compile-time constants, or decompression output is budgeted.
public_references: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/409.html
CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/119.html
Python documentation: integer string conversion length limitation — https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#int-max-str-digits
